tools.name: get_resolve_status
tools.description: Check whether DaVinci Resolve is currently running and reachable, and report its version.

options.instructions: Call this first in a session to confirm the connection before reading or changing a project.

tools.name: launch_resolve
tools.description: Launch DaVinci Resolve and wait for it to be ready (60 second timeout).

options.instructions: Use only when get_resolve_status reports the application is not running. Starting the application is slow; wait for it to finish opening before inspecting a project.

tools.name: get_whats_new
tools.description: Returns DaVinci Resolve changelog entries introduced after the version or date you already know, so features newer than your training data are not missed.

since.description: Last version you know (e.g. "19.0") or last ISO date you were trained on (e.g. "2025-01-25").

options.instructions: Call once before planning an unfamiliar workflow; Resolve adds major features between releases.

tools.name: search_scripting_api
tools.description: Search the installed Python API stubs and return the matching types and functions with their descriptions. The pattern is a case-insensitive regular expression.

pattern.description: Case-insensitive Python regular expression, e.g. "marker" or "(Get|Set)Setting".

options.instructions: Cheapest way to discover the current API. Search here before writing any run_script body, and never guess a method name or signature from memory.

tools.name: get_scripting_api
tools.description: Return the installed Python stubs for the DaVinci Resolve, Fusion or Fusion UI API, whole, as an outline, for selected types, or written to a file whose path is returned.

types.description: Return only these top-level definitions, e.g. ["Timeline", "TimelineItem"].

outline.description: Return only the list of top-level definitions with their descriptions.

as_file.description: Write the whole stub to a file and return its path instead of its contents.

options.instructions: Use outline=true or types=[...] instead of fetching a whole 163 KiB stub. Use as_file=true when you can read and grep local files, then read the returned path.

tools.name: get_scripting_docs
tools.description: Return DaVinci Resolve developer documentation, in full or one section: the scripting guide, the DCTL language reference, or the Fusion tool list and reference.

section.description: Markdown heading to return; default "TOC", empty string for the whole document.

as_file.description: Write the document to a file and return its path instead of its contents.

options.instructions: Ask for the TOC first, then one section. FusionToolReference.md is 1.3 MiB, so always use a section or as_file=true for it.

tools.name: run_script
tools.description: Execute a sandboxed Python script with the DaVinciResolveScript API. `resolve` and `project` are provided; assign your output to `result` to return structured data.

options.instructions: The main editing tool: nearly every project, timeline, media pool and render operation goes through here. Discover the API with search_scripting_api first, keep the script short, and set `result` to a JSON-serialisable dict. Read the state before changing it, and re-read afterwards to confirm the intended clips or ranges actually changed.

tools.name: run_script_unsafe
tools.description: Execute an unrestricted Python script with the DaVinciResolveScript API plus full filesystem, network and subprocess access. Disabled by default.

options.instructions: Disabled on purpose: it bypasses the sandbox around run_script. Enable it in Settings only for a task that genuinely needs file or network access, and prefer an Aworkit file tool for plain file work.

tools.name: describe_grade
tools.description: Describe what the nodes of a grade contain, per node, instead of rendering frames and comparing them by eye. Sources: the clip under the playhead, the timeline grade, or the current photo.

timecode.description: Timeline timecode "HH:MM:SS:FF" for a clip other than the one under the playhead. The playhead is never moved.

track.description: 1-based video track, counting from the bottom as V1 does.

options.instructions: Prefer this over get_image when the question is what a grade contains (nodes, LUTs, tools, CDLs) rather than what it looks like.

tools.name: get_image
tools.description: Return a rendered, graded and color-managed frame as an image, plus basic grade and color science information. Supports a region of interest for detail.

timecode.description: Timeline timecode "HH:MM:SS:FF"; defaults to the playhead, which is never moved.

frame_offset.description: 0-based frame offset into the source; an alternative to timecode for source "timeline".

max_dimension.description: Caps the longer edge in pixels (max 4096).

roi_x.description: Left edge of the region as a fraction of the frame width.

roi_y.description: Top edge of the region as a fraction of the frame height.

roi_width.description: Region width as a fraction of the frame width.

roi_height.description: Region height as a fraction of the frame height.

options.instructions: Use media_pool_clip as the ungraded before reference and timeline for the graded after. Crop with the roi_* fractions to inspect detail at max_dimension instead of raising the resolution.

tools.name: get_thumbnails
tools.description: Return thumbnail frames of one source as a single labelled grid image, for judging a shot, a range or an album at a glance.

count.description: How many frames to show, 1 to 48.

start.description: First frame of the span, 0-based offset or "HH:MM:SS:FF" for source "timeline".

end.description: Last frame of the span, in the same form as start.

max_dimension.description: Caps the longer edge of the whole sheet in pixels (max 4096).

options.instructions: Prefer one grid over repeated get_image calls when the question spans a range. Cell labels are the timecodes that get_image takes to render one full size.

tools.name: list_luts
tools.description: List LUT and DCTL files recursively in the global LUT directory.

options.instructions: Check which LUTs and DCTLs already exist before generating or writing one.

tools.name: read_dctl
tools.description: Return the source of a .dctl file in the global LUT directory.

path.description: File name relative to the global LUT directory, e.g. "MCP/cool.dctl".

options.instructions: Read an existing DCTL before editing it, so the whole file is rewritten rather than partly reconstructed.

tools.name: write_dctl
tools.description: Compile and write (or overwrite) a .dctl file in the MCP LUT directory. A DCTL resolves as a node in the grader.

options.instructions: Read the DCTL reference with get_scripting_docs document "DCTLReadme.txt" first. Writing an existing name overwrites that file.

tools.name: generate_lut
tools.description: Generate a .cube 3D LUT by evaluating a sandboxed Python transform function on every lattice point, written to the MCP LUT directory.

size.description: Cube size per axis, e.g. 33. Common values: 17, 33, 65.

transform.description: Python function body receiving r, g, b floats in [0,1] and returning an (r, g, b) tuple. math is pre-imported.

options.instructions: Keep the transform algebraically simple and monotonic; a 65-point cube is 274k evaluations, so state clearly which size you chose and why.

tools.name: delete_lut_file
tools.description: Delete a LUT or DCTL file from the MCP LUT directory, identified by its extension.

options.instructions: Only delete a file you created in this session unless the user named it explicitly; list_luts first to confirm the exact name.

tools.name: list_extras_packages
tools.description: List Extras Download Manager packages available for this Resolve version with their installation status. Some scripting API calls need them (mostly AI models).

options.instructions: Check here when a scripting call reports a missing model or package.

tools.name: install_extras_package
tools.description: Queue downloading and installing Extras Download Manager packages named exactly as list_extras_packages reports them.

names.description: Package names exactly as reported by list_extras_packages.

options.instructions: Ask the user before starting a download: these are large. Poll list_extras_packages for progress.
